assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos with a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector opened neutrino astronomy and addressed the long-standing question of cosmic-ray origins. It is an original, instrument-driven discovery with a clear outcome, which fits my own experimental astroparticle perspective.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and the 2013 observation, so a one-name proposal is defensible from the supplied credit. A discovery of this kind rests on a large collaboration and on predecessors such as AMANDA and early theoretical flux arguments, and I cannot tell from the longlist whether a fair configuration needs additional names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the diffuse flux has been confirmed in several independent channels, and later results (the multimessenger association with a blazar in 2017-2018, the Galactic-plane neutrinos in 2023) strengthen it. Timing looks right.
uncertainties: Credit is a single name for a collaboration-scale discovery; the allocation to other founders is unresolved in the supplied text.
I cannot independently verify the details of the later source associations and rely on my recollection of them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices turned strongly interacting many-body systems into tunable laboratory simulators, with the superfluid to Mott insulator transition as the benchmark. The idea has influenced condensed-matter, atomic and quantum-information physics broadly, and its impact is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac supplied foundational theory for lattice quantum simulation, and Bloch led a leading experimental programme. Greiner (an early Mott insulator experiment) and Dalibard are strong claimants, and decisive experimental credit also involves people not on this list, so any three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Mature: roughly twenty-five years of independent confirmation across many groups, now including quantum gas microscopes and quantitative simulation results. Recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Experimental credit for the first Mott insulator realisation is divided and includes people beyond the supplied names.
Other list entries credit Cirac and Zoller, which could complicate a combined prize configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by observation in HgTe quantum wells, created a new classification of band structure that reshaped condensed-matter physics. The concept is original and clear and has long-lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical predictions; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation, guided by a separate theory proposal (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang) whose authors are not among the credited names. The supplied three can support a clean prize, but that omission is a real fairness issue.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent confirmation exists in HgTe and in three-dimensional materials, and the framework has been stable for about twenty years. Timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The authors of the HgTe proposal that guided the experiment are outside the supplied names.
Closely related three-dimensional topological insulator work could blur the scope of a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED showed strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave resonators, providing the architecture for superconducting quantum processors and quantum-limited measurement. Its impact is substantial and its mechanism is clear.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff share the central 2004 proposal and demonstration. Four names exceed the three-laureate limit, so I choose the theory proposer and the two experimental leaders and leave Girvin out; that exclusion is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced, with a large research and industrial ecosystem. Timing is somewhat delicate because I believe the 2025 physics prize went to closely related superconducting-circuit work, though I have not verified this independently.
uncertainties: Four credited names for a three-person limit; Girvin's exclusion is contestable.
Proximity to a recent superconducting-circuit prize may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of magic-angle flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moire quantum materials. The idea is original and has produced a large, fast-growing literature.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive correlated-state discoveries together with junior co-authors. The three names give a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, though credit for the experimental co-first authors is a question.
assessment.maturity: Comparatively young: the main experimental results date from 2018, and the interpretation of the superconducting and correlated phases is still debated. The discovery is solid but recognition may be early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated phases remain unsettled.
Experimental credit beyond the group leader is not supported by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing is a new-window result with deep implications for supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly new physics. It builds on decades of precise timing instrumentation, which is close to my own experience.
assessment.attribution: Several timing-array collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and others) reported the signal. The three named people represent different arrays, but a prize would have to choose among many founders and teams, so the credit allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the Hellings-Downs correlation was seen at a significance below the conventional discovery threshold as I recall it, the astrophysical source is not identified, and combined independent analyses are still maturing.
uncertainties: Statistical significance is moderate and the interpretation (binary black holes or cosmological sources) is open.
Credit across several collaborations cannot be settled by three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation and the quantum generation of primordial perturbations explain flatness, horizon uniformity and the seed spectrum of structure, and the framework has shaped modern cosmology. Its conceptual originality and consequences are very high.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde and Mukhanov are credited, but others (for example Starobinsky, Albrecht, Steinhardt and Sato) made decisive contributions to the model or the perturbation calculation, so no fair three-person split is guaranteed.
assessment.maturity: The CMB spectrum agrees with inflationary predictions, but there is no direct detection of primordial gravitational waves and no unique model, so empirical confirmation is indirect. As an experimentalist I regard recognition as premature.
uncertainties: No primordial B-mode detection; alternatives are not excluded.
Priority between several groups is disputed, and I am unsure of some details of the early history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS detectors made the Higgs boson discovery possible, and the instrument concepts are technological achievements of the first rank. I value this as an instrument builder, but a prize would honour detector design rather than a discovery of a physical phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were founding proposers and spokespersons, so a three-person split is supportable. Credit for the detectors is shared among thousands of collaboration members, and the chosen names are leadership representatives.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the detectors have delivered over a decade of validated results. However, the Higgs discovery itself was recognised in 2013, and honouring a detector-building effort sits at the edge of the prize criteria.
uncertainties: Whether prize tradition favours recognising collaboration leadership for instrumentation is unclear.
The earlier prize already covers the physics outcome.
